reason: Runtime is fine but the design does not discriminate as written. (1) Controls are mis-specified: Q-irreducibility of Psi does not depend on ord_n(2). Measured with gp (Koblitz t=+-1, Psi=P(T^n)/(T^2-tT+2)): n=11,17,31,131 all Psi irreducible; n=17 (ord 8) and n=31 (ord 5) are irreducible, contradicting the stated control prediction 'split into ord_n(2)-blocks'; n=7 splits only because sqrt(-7) in Q(zeta_7) (Q(zeta*tau) has degree 6 not 12), unrelated to 2-primitivity. ord_n(2) governs F_2[T]/(T^n-1) factorisation (F_2-linear Frobenius-stable subspaces), a different object. Hypothesis 'ord_n(2)=n-1' is unnecessary for the simplicity claim; proof needs only n prime, n!=7, tau/taubar not a root of unity. (2) Random-E arm is near-vacuous: for prime n, T^n-alpha is irreducible over K=Q(alpha) unless alpha is an n-th power in K, which forces norm-2 beta, i.e. E a base change from F_2 (j in {0,1}); a random E never hits this, so 200 curves x 10 n give 100% irreducible with no power to detect failure. Also supersingular/a even must be excluded. (3) Scaling is unnecessary: n=131 is directly computable (polisirreducible on deg-262 and deg-260 integer polys, ms; verified Psi irreducible at 131 for both Koblitz twists). (4) Metric is structural (irreducibility bit, factor degrees), not wall time: good. Runtime: Koblitz arm and n=131 <1 s; random-E arm needs ellcard over F_{2^n}, which was slow in this sandbox (>2 min for 6 n values x 15 curves incl. n<=19), so 200 curves x n up to 83 is not within 2 CPU-min and is also unnecessary.
fix: Replace with: (A) Exact Koblitz arm at every prime n<=131 (and n=131 itself), both twists t=+-1: a_n via recurrence s_k=t*s_{k-1}-2*s_{k-2} (NOT P(T^n) of the F_2-poly), Q=T^{2n}-a_n*T^n+2^n, report factor degrees of Q and of Q/(T^2-tT+2); prediction: Psi irreducible for all prime n!=7 independent of ord_n(2); n=7 is the sole expected exception (sqrt(-7) in Q(zeta_7)). Also check n composite (e.g. 9,15,21) as positive controls for reducibility via T^n-alpha factoring. (B) Replace the random-E arm by a targeted positive control: E with alpha=beta^n (take F_2-curve base-changed; and a twist/isogenous non-F_2 curve with alpha a perfect n-th power in K if any), plus randomness only via a symbolic argument: loop over integer traces a with |a|<2^{n/2+1}, a odd, using only the Weil polynomial (no point counting): test polisirreducible(T^{2n}-aT^n+2^n) for n in {11,13,19,29,37,53,59,61,67,83,131} over a random sample of 2000 a plus a=+-t_k from Koblitz; reducible iff alpha is an n-th power in K, so also test via nfroots/ispower in K and confirm agreement. (C) Null/disagreement arm: assert polisirreducible result == (not ispower(alpha, n) in K) for all sampled a. (D) Relabel the F_2-linear-subspace statement: ord_n(2) blocks belong to a separate F_2[T]/(T^n-1) test (factormod(T^n-1,2)); report both so 'no subfield' and 'simplicity' are not conflated. Add caveat: F_2-simplicity of Res does not imply simplicity over F_{2^n} (Res splits to prod of Galois conjugates of E there), so 'no non-product sub-abelian variety' holds only over F_2; Prym quotients over F_{2^n} are not excluded by this certificate. Classification: theory/relabelling (no advance); lower bound genus>=n-1 for a carrier Jacobian J with Res as F_2-isogeny factor holds only if J is over F_2 and Res is a factor, which this experiment does not test.
